Our understanding and proposed approach

Our understanding

Kilbride Veterinary Group runs three clinics in Navan, Trim and Kells. You have 11 vets and 19 support staff. Phones are a major pressure point. You receive about 640 inbound calls a week. Orla estimates that about 38% of after-hours calls go unanswered or to voicemail that is not checked until morning.

Most calls are routine. About half are appointment bookings and changes. Others are repeat prescriptions and questions about whether a call is an emergency. Emergencies must reach the on-call vet immediately. This is non-negotiable.

You want an assistant to answer after hours, book routine appointments, send reminders, and route anything that might be an emergency straight to the on-call vet's mobile.

Your practice management system is VetLink 4. It does not allow other systems to connect to it directly. Bookings would need to be handled through a daily export and import, or entered by staff by hand.

You would like it in use before the spring vaccination rush in March 2027. Budget was not discussed. It is to be confirmed with Orla and the two partners. Client records include owner names, addresses and phone numbers. The storage location for call recordings is to be confirmed.

Proposed approach

We propose a six-week pilot at Trim, the smallest clinic. This will let us test the service in one location before extending it to all three clinics. The pilot start date is to be confirmed.

The assistant will answer after-hours calls. It will take routine appointment bookings and changes. It will send reminders. It will identify calls that may be emergencies and route them straight to the on-call vet's mobile.

For bookings, we will use the method that works with VetLink 4. This may be a daily export and import, or staff entering bookings by hand. The best method is to be confirmed during the pilot.

We will confirm where call recordings will be stored. We will also confirm budget with Orla and the partners.

Action list

1. Sinead: Finish all 4,000 Murphy's Bakery boxes. Due: Friday afternoon, 14 November 2026.
2. Tomasz: Book courier for Monday delivery of Murphy's Bakery boxes. Due: Thursday 13 November 2026.
3. Tomasz: Send Murphy's Bakery boxes by courier. Due: Monday 16 November 2026.
4. Aoife: Ring Clarke & Sons finance person about the €8,420 invoice, 67 days overdue. Due: Tuesday 17 November 2026.
5. Aoife: Tell Declan if Clarke & Sons do not commit to a date. Due: to be confirmed.
6. Declan: Ring Michael Clarke if Clarke & Sons do not commit to a date. Due: to be confirmed.
7. Owner to be confirmed: Chase blue ink supplier. Due: to be confirmed.
8. Declan: Send Christmas closing dates. Due: end of next week.

Email

Subject: Follow-up: operations meeting, 13 November 2026

Hi all,

Thanks for the short meeting.

Sinead will finish the 4,000 Murphy's Bakery boxes by Friday afternoon. Tomasz will book a courier today and send the boxes on Monday. The van is off the road until 21 November 2026 at the earliest.

Aoife will ring Clarke & Sons about the €8,420 invoice by Tuesday. If they do not commit to a date, she will tell Declan. Declan will then ring Michael Clarke.

No owner was agreed for chasing the blue ink supplier. This is to be confirmed. Blue ink stock is about two weeks' supply.

Declan will send the Christmas closing dates by end of next week.

Please reply if any detail is wrong.

Regards,

Dear Ms Doyle,

Thank you for your email. I am sorry for the problems with your kitchen installation. I am also sorry for the time you took off work.

On 6 November, our scheduler double-booked the two-person fitting team onto another job. This was our fault. Nobody rang you. I am sorry.

On 7 November, one fitter arrived to start the work. The quartz worktops had not arrived from our supplier. The supplier caused the delay. However, we knew on 5 November that the worktops would not arrive. We should have told you then. We did not. That was our fault.

Your new fitting date is to be confirmed once the worktops arrive. The supplier now says the week of 24 November.

Your deposit of €2,400 is non-refundable once materials are ordered. Your materials were ordered on 20 October. I cannot promise a refund. I will send your refund request to the operations manager.

As a goodwill gesture, I can offer you a €150 account credit or voucher. Please tell me which you prefer.

Your named contact is Ardee Kitchens Customer Care.

Yours sincerely,  
Ardee Kitchens Customer Care

Subject: Hybrid working policy from 1 January 2027

Dear all,

This policy applies from 1 January 2027.

It applies to employees whose role can be done remotely in part, as agreed with their line manager. Employees in their first six months are not eligible. They work from the office full time.

You must work in the Galway office for at least two days each week. One day must be Tuesday, the team day. Your line manager agrees your second office day.

You must be available between 10:00 and 15:00, whether at home or in the office.

Hybrid working starts only after both of these are done:

- your line manager approves it in writing;
- you complete the home-office health and safety self-assessment form.

How to get or submit the self-assessment form is to be confirmed.

The company provides a laptop and headset. A one-off home-office allowance of up to €300 is paid on receipts for a desk, chair or monitor.

The company does not reimburse travel between home and the office. It does not pay home utility bills.

You must not print confidential client drawings at home.

The company may review or withdraw hybrid working for any employee or team. It will give four weeks' written notice. This may happen if business needs change or performance drops.

Questions: hr@corrib-eng.example

HR

Board summary – Q3 2026

Group revenue was €1,614 thousand in Q3 2026. This was €16 thousand lower than Q3 2025. Gross margin fell from 40.5% to 38.6%. The decline came from Athlone.

Mullingar and Tullamore grew revenue. Mullingar revenue rose from €612 thousand to €655 thousand. Its margin fell from 41.0% to 40.2%. Tullamore revenue rose from €488 thousand to €503 thousand. Its margin fell from 39.5% to 38.9%.

Athlone revenue fell from €530 thousand to €456 thousand. Its margin fell from 40.8% to 36.1%. The finance manager says the drop followed the opening of a competitor from a national chain 2 kilometres away in June 2026. Athlone also used heavier discounting in August to hold customer numbers. This explains most of its margin fall.

Online click-and-collect started in May. It is included in each store's figures. It is not reported separately. There were no one-off items in either year.

To be confirmed: customer numbers by store, online click-and-collect sales, costs, and any plan to respond to the Athlone competitor.

Subject: Client portal outage on Friday 14 November 2026

Dear Client,

Our client portal was unavailable from 08:55 to 14:55 on Friday 14 November 2026. Browsers showed a security warning.

The cause was an expired security certificate. Automatic renewal had failed since October because of a changed technical record. The certificate was renewed at 10:40. Some users still saw errors. All checks passed by 14:55. The portal is fully available. The disruption lasted about six hours.

There was no unauthorised access. The expired certificate blocked connections. It did not expose data. Our IT provider reviewed the logs.

Four client uploads made between 08:50 and 08:55 did not complete. Those clients have been identified. They must resubmit their documents. They will be contacted individually by Monday 17 November.

We now monitor certificate renewals. An alert now goes to two people 30 days before any certificate expires.

No deadlines were affected. The 14 November ROS filing for affected clients was completed by staff by phone or email.

Contact details for follow-up are to be confirmed.

Feeney & Walsh Chartered Accountants

Office Manager  
Gallagher Quinn Solicitors, Dundalk

We are a small practice. We have three partners, four solicitors and five support staff. We mainly do conveyancing, probate and family law.

We are looking for an Office Manager to run the office day to day. You will supervise the two receptionists. You will manage the diary system, closing and archiving files, supplier contracts, and contact with our outside IT provider. You will also manage the accounts system for client money. Training will be given. You must be comfortable with numbers and confidentiality.

You need at least three years in an office management or senior administrative role. Legal experience is a plus, but not required.

Salary: €42,000 to €46,000, depending on experience.

Hours: 9:00 to 17:30, Monday to Friday. One evening a week, on Thursday, you will work on reception until 19:00 for late appointments. You will get time off to make up the hours.

After a six-month probation, one day a week from home may be possible.

Pension details are to be confirmed with the partners.

Start date: January 2027.

To apply, send your CV and a short cover note to careers@gqsolicitors.example by 5 December 2026.

Subject: Linen and laundry agreement - points to check

Dear [Name],

I am not a solicitor. Please ask a solicitor to review the agreement before you sign. I can only summarise the extract.

The agreement starts on 1 March 2025. It runs for 24 months. After that, it renews automatically for 12 months at a time. Either side must give written notice at least 90 days before the renewal date to stop renewal.

During the term, you must get all linen hire and laundry services for the Premises only from Brightwash.

Charges can rise each year on the start date. The rise is CPI plus 3 percentage points. The maximum rise is 8% in any year.

You must pay for at least 900 kg of laundry each month. This applies even if you use less.

Brightwash's responsibility for losses is limited to the charges you paid in the 12 months before a claim. It is not responsible for loss of business or loss of profits. This includes late delivery.

A solicitor can check whether these terms suit your business. The extract does not say how notice must be given. It does not say what happens if the 90-day deadline is missed. It does not say what "Premises" covers. It does not say whether linen hire counts toward the 900 kg. These need to be confirmed.

Kind regards,  
[Name]

To: Managing Director  
Subject: CRM replacement for Shannon Freight Forwarding (25 users)

Recommendation  
Choose Option B: Larchmont CRM.

Reason  
Gerard says the Xero link is essential. The accounts team re-key every invoice today. Larchmont has a built-in Xero link. Pipewell needs Zapier at about €60 per month. This adds cost.

Annual cost  
Option A: €18 x 25 users x 12 months = €5,400. Add Zapier: €60 x 12 = €720. Total: about €6,120.  
Option B: €29 x 25 users x 12 months = €8,700.  
Option B costs about €2,580 more each year.

Trade-offs  
Option A is cheaper. It is monthly and can be cancelled any time. In a two-week trial, four of six staff preferred its interface. But it has no built-in Xero link. We would set up customs fields. That needs about three days of Ciara’s time. We would import the data ourselves. Support is email only during business hours.

Option B costs more. It needs a 12-month minimum commitment. Two of six staff preferred it. But it has a built-in Xero link. It has a customs-document template. The vendor moves the data. It is included. Support includes phone and email during business hours.

To be confirmed  
The cost of Ciara’s three days is to be confirmed. The reliability of the Zapier link is to be confirmed. The time needed to import data under Option A is to be confirmed.

Reilly Joinery in Cavan makes custom kitchens and wardrobes. It has 14 staff.

Quotes took about three working days. The owner, Fintan Reilly, priced every job from scratch in a spreadsheet.

We built a quoting template from their last 200 jobs. Standard units and finishes were priced in. We trained the office manager to use it. The work took six weeks and finished in September 2026.

Now about 70% of quotes go out the same day. The other 30% involve unusual layouts or bespoke finishes. They still need the owner and take about as long as before.

Fintan Reilly, owner: "Most quotes go out the same day now. Not every job fits the template, and that's fine - those are the ones that need me anyway."

Revenue and win-rate figures are to be confirmed.
